_meta.description: Per-sector unit-economics benchmarks from published industry research. Replaces a generated file in which ltv_estimate was exactly 10x cac_estimate for every sector, churn was a flat 0.05 and break_even_months a flat 24 - constants that gave the appearance of sector differentiation while providing none.

fields.churn_estimate: Median monthly customer churn, as a fraction (0.096 = 9.6% per month).
fields.cac_payback_months: Median months to recover the acquisition cost of ONE customer. This is NOT the point at which the business becomes profitable.
fields.reference_cac_usd: Median CAC in USD for the cited segment. Reference only - the app computes CAC from the budget and does not read this field.
fields.basis: Which published segment the figures are taken from, and where a proxy was used.

_meta.caveat: These are industry medians, not measurements of any specific venture. A pre-revenue startup has no observed churn or CAC; these describe what comparable companies report. CAC payback and business break-even are different things and are reported separately; neither is a measurement of any specific venture.

corrections_2026_09_18.roi_estimate_removed: Every sector carried roi_estimate identical to its ltv_cac_ratio, and the app multiplied it by 100 and blended it into ROI - so an LTV:CAC of 3.0 was reported as a 300% return. Those are different quantities: LTV:CAC compares one customer's lifetime value to the cost of acquiring them, while ROI is a return on the whole invested capital. The field was a mislabelled duplicate and is removed; ltv_cac_ratio is now surfaced as itself.
corrections_2026_09_18.break_even_renamed: break_even_months held what the cited sources publish, which is CAC payback, and the app blended it with a model prediction of business break-even. Averaging a 4-month payback with a 15-month break-even produced a number that measured neither. Renamed to cac_payback_months and reported in its own right; business break-even now comes from the model alone.
corrections_2026_09_18.fields_block_was_wrong: The previous fields block documented churn_monthly_pct and payback_months, neither of which existed in the data, and omitted the two fields that did.

ai.basis: B2B SaaS, self-serve / product-led growth segment.

tech.basis: B2B SaaS, self-serve / product-led growth segment.

e-commerce.basis: Direct-to-consumer ecommerce; churn from subscription-box DTC, which reports 7-10% monthly.
e-commerce.source: Klipfolio DTC Benchmarks; Recurly churn research

edtech.basis: EdTech SaaS, the highest-churn vertical measured. LTV:CAC uses the 3.0 cross-industry consensus floor, as no EdTech-specific ratio is published.
edtech.source: RetentionCheck churn benchmarks; Userpilot CAC benchmarks

fintech.basis: Consumer fintech. B2B fintech CAC is far higher (median USD 3,160).

healthcare.basis: Regulated verticals (healthcare IT, legal tech) churn 30-50% below horizontal SaaS on high switching costs; 2.1% is the midpoint of that reduction applied to the 3.5% SaaS median. No healthcare-specific CAC is published.

gaming.basis: Mobile gaming CAC is published; churn and LTV:CAC are not, so churn uses the consumer-app range and the ratio uses the 3.0 consensus floor. Treat both as placeholders, not measurements.

foodtech.basis: PROXY: no foodtech-specific benchmark is published, so this uses direct-to-consumer ecommerce, the nearest measured category.

logistics.basis: PROXY: B2B services / agency segment, the nearest measured category to logistics.

energy.basis: PROXY: no energy/cleantech unit-economics benchmark is published. Uses the 3.0 cross-industry consensus floor and a long payback reflecting capital intensity. The weakest-supported entry in this file.
